title: Bounded-box reductions in the Subbarao-Warren problem for unitary perfect numbers
summary: A unitary perfect number is a positive integer n satisfying σ^*(n)=2n, where σ^* sums unitary divisors. Only five examples are known, and no sixth has been found. We revisit the Subbarao-Warren problem by keeping the seed factor 2^a+1 explicit in the full balance (2^a+1)\prod_i(p_i^{e_i}+1)=2^{a+1}\prod_i p_i^{e_i}. Within a bounded enumeration of source components in the odd dependency graph, every admissible source kernel is either one of the two kernels occurring in the known nonsquarefree examples, 3^2 and 5^4, or one of five additional impostor kernels.
